Return to Periapt had been an internet rumor, a creepypasta about a cursed computer game hidden on an old CD-ROM that could be found in the strangest of places. The game was about explorers on a wild continent of magic beasts, wagon trains, and deadly trails. They said it felt real, and that if you played long enough, it would actually be real.

Hollis Hood knew it was no mere rumor. He knew why people called it cursed and about the oath that let you leave your world behind. He knew all this because when he was a kid, he played the game, and when it offered him an escape from his life, he said no.

It was a choice that haunted him for fifteen years.

After a long search, he found another copy. This time, he was prepared. He trained, planned, and shaped his life around the chance he once abandoned. He followed the cursed game's lead all the way to Periapt, prepared to protect the settlers as they headed into its wild interior. But he arrived at the starting town to find it abandoned and plagued by a fog that consumes all that are caught in its wake.

What he didn't foresee was that the adventure did not wait for him.

Sure, he arrived prepared, but he also arrived far too late.

What to Expect:

 >Dark Fantasy LitRPG inspired by classic 90s CRPGs and dungeon crawlers

 >A power system where magic comes from plants, beasts, and ecosystems

 >Animal bonding with consequences. Animals and plants are companions, magical resources, and meals

 >Meaningful progression through creature bonds, body augmentation, and crafting

 >Grim frontier survival with 1800s-era tech and creeping horror

 >Structured arcs with real conclusions, not endless filler

If you like slow-burn power growth, dangerous worlds that don’t forgive mistakes, and progression earned through hard choices, Periapt is waiting.

Kaius just wanted to unlock his class - instead, he restarted the apocalypse.

After years of training, Kaius has barely acquired the first two of his family's legacy skills. Powerful and vanishingly rare, the method of creating them is a secret people would kill for.

When she woke up in her favorite otome video game, she wasn't expecting to open the eyes of Gerda the npc troll. 

It's been five years. Five long, intense years of leveling up and dungeon delving and treasure hunting and working her butt off to give everyone the happily ever after her favorite characters deserved. And she's managed well so far. 

Season two is coming to a close, and the final season almost upon her. There are dragons in her future, and something even more terrifying: a lot of walking. Can she help her stan find love? Can she complete her work and find a way home? And can she hide the fact that she is Madame Potts? 

...

Julian van Slyke watched his father die to protect their home in the revolution twenty years ago in a battle that split the country into a grand ravine... and he's been working hard to walk in those footsteps ever since. 

To grow strong, he's been guarding the border to the Untamed Ice Fields, where a dungeon break sends out monsters to challenge their defenses in surges. He is determined to find the dungeon and defeat it, and prove to himself that he is ready to take over the duchy. 

Now his home is being threatened by Blackfog spies, portents of doom are keeping him too long from the border, and he's caught up in something much bigger than he can understand. Not only that, he keeps tripping on Gerda no matter where he turns. Can he keep everyone safe? Can he conquer the dungeon his father didn't? And can he resist teasing a certain bridge troll? 

A cozy LitRPG romcom reminiscent of the Bridgertons, with masquerade balls, fireballs, and butternut rumballs.

Frank isn’t exactly a model citizen. He's also not here to save Earth; he just wants his favorite curse word back. Too bad the World Dungeon drops him in as a zombie with a level cap of 1 and a profanity filter that turns every F-bomb into “frank.”

Earth is repossessed and rebranded by a mega corp called DungeonCore. The prize is ownership of the planet. This season is Hardcore Mode: if he dies, he gets stuck in his Lair until the next expansion drops, losing everything but the account unlocks he’s scraped together. Every death adds growing galactic debt to cover his auto-respawn fees. Humanity gets a head start, but deep-pocketed aliens are lining up to buy their way in.

To make matters worse, some corporate genius hands all the hero classes to the NPCs, while actual players get saddled with monster classes. Frank spawns as a lowly zombie. All he’s got is stubbornness, handyman’s grit, and an accidental Universe First achievement that lets him build a class of his own.

Frank’s no hero; he’s not even alive, technically. However, he is petty enough to move mountains if it means unlocking one four-letter word. Will that be enough to win? Probably not. But it might be enough to swear again.

Level One Zombie is a darkly funny, System-forward LitRPG with Lair/town building, bureaucratic satire, and a delightfully petty anti-hero.

What to expect:
Single POV, first-person, past-tense
Cursing, and lots of it
Deeply flawed, badass, anti-hero, male MC
Dark themes (which are neither fetishized nor glorified)
Lair building with worker and resource management
Themed Instances (dungeons) with interesting boss fights
Crunchy LitRPG with System messages and loads of stats and menus

What not to expect:
Romance

Chapter length:
2k to 2.5k

Schedule:
Mon, Thur @ 7:05 am EST

An unshackled killer cyborg ends up terminating her way through...ahem ‘exploring’ fantasyland with a dungeon core power source!  A lighthearted super-OP misunderstanding-filled Isekai LitRPG adventure!

A note on spinoffs and spoilers: This novel is technically a spinoff of my other novel, The Faceless Minion, however I intend for it to be standalone and so will attempt to write it in such a way that will not require you to have read the other first.  There might be some slight, unavoidable spoilers in the premise if you are not fully up to date on The Faceless Minion (chapter 187 to be precise) and if you read that one first the backstory of the premise will make more sense and you will start off more invested in the MC, but it should not be necessary to enjoy this novel.  With that out of the way, let’s begin!

Non-Standard Leashed-Intelligence Cybernetic Enforcer, Designation: NSLICE-00P, was your average, everyday killer cyborg enslaved to a shadow organization bent on world domination in a superhero universe…that is until she ended up getting hacked, sent back in time, and ordered to terminate her own creator!

And once she succeeded, the resulting time paradox ejected her from her reality!

Now the wayward cyborg girl/living superweapon finds herself in a strange new world…with no directives.  No knowledge.  No commanders.  No shadow organizations.  No way home.

But with new and fantastic powers.

What could possibly go wrong?

Note that though the MC has dungeon powers, we won’t be focusing on dungeon construction or management (at least to start off, later plot TBD).  We’re terminating the other world, not turtling in the other world!

The Federation of Man is desperately lacking a proper supervillain. 

Luckily for them, there might just be one on the rise.

Luke was fine with being a cashier, watching Villainy be made a mockery of by amateurs.

But after being robbed, electrocuted, robbed, beaten and then robbed again all in the same week some screws might've gotten knocked loose. Because the state of Villainy is not fine, and Luke's bored, crazy and stupid enough to believe he can change it. 

And apparently, some mystic jackass named the Architect thinks so too, planting a system on Luke that only wants one thing from him. 

Evil... done right!

**********

The gods don't play dice with the universe; they play Board & Conquest.

Wepwawet, young god of wolves and scouts, is given a task to prove himself worthy of becoming a major god: form a new pantheon with other junior deities, manage a young civilization on a newborn world, and train mortal Champions to resist an inevitable Titan Incursion. 

Being saddled with an ice-covered barbarian village besieged from all sides isn’t ideal, but it's now his duty to transform this ragtag bunch of misfits into the most formidable force the world of Elphion has ever seen. “I offer you an adventure. In a world of magic and monsters, steel and fire, ruins and long forgotten fates. If you are willing.”

 

 

Veron was fed up with his corporate job in Paris. He quit and moved to the countryside, taking a step back to take a breath, to think about where his path had led him, and what he wanted now. When he decides to take a nap in one of the quiet countryside forests, he spots something strange. A hazy glowing bird of light, very interested in getting him to follow. And of course, he bites.

What he finds is an offer. No demon king to slay, no rebellion to lead, nor gods looking for a pawn. An adventure, that is all. Just Veron, and the magic that he learns to wield.

He is sent to Renavor and arrives in a mountainous valley, ready to explore a world on the brink of change, with relics unearthed in ancient dungeons, and beasts of blood and chaos lurking in the dark.

Shelter would come first, and then he could figure out the rest.

 

What to expect: Journey to Veresavir is an isekai fantasy and progression story with litrpg elements. The litrpg aspect is very light at the start, so no massive stat screens or tons of skills. It will increase later in the story. The pacing is neither particularly fast nor slow, though the power progression itself is slow.

The main themes are magic discovery, exploration, action, slice of life, monster hunts/dungeoneering, survival, friendship, and self-discovery.

The tone and stakes of the novel vary depending on what happens (what a basic thing to say). What I mean by that is that it’s hard for me to pin down an overall feel. There will be chill slice of life focused chapters, chill fights, but also high stakes scenes and sections with fear, grief, and tension at the forefront. I would say it’s balanced.

I’m the author of Azarinth Healer, and if you read it or a part of it, here’s a quick thought of comparison. Veresavir is slower, more grounded, and more mature. The progression and magic isn’t as flashy but it’s still my voice, and everything I learned. I think no matter if you liked Azarinth or not, give this one a chance, I like it a lot :)!
